findings.issue: Only the definition was made balanced. The ledger, the advice and the edge are the catalyst page unchanged. **16 of 25** Balanced advices open by saying the reader runs short ("Your light runs short", P156; "Your drive is short", P167; "Your mind takes in less than it could use", P171; "What you have to give runs short", P174, and so on). Then each gives three acts to *grow* the energy under the verdict "Keep the mix." A Balanced reader sees all five pages balanced. A Balanced Wood-core reader (P151, P156, P161, P166, P171) is therefore told on every page that they run short, which no chart can be. In addition, **8 pages** have a balanced tail that the shown persona's keywords contradict on the same screen: P154, P158 ("You learn from others" vs "Self-taught is the only learning you trust"), P161, P163, P167, P169, P173, P175. About 6 more contradict it mildly (P153, P157, P159, P165, P166, P174). Two Balanced ledger passages still state a thin chart as the cause (P154 "Carrying less Wood than drive to spend", P175 "Little Water comes in").
findings.fix: Rule, three parts. (1) **A balanced advice per pair cell** (25 texts, ≤60 words). The diagnosis names the balance and what tips it, and one or two *keep* acts draw on the element. Never "runs short", never an act to grow. Example, 木_木: "Your strength takes in about as much as it gives, and one long push is what tips it. Keep your weekly training through the busy months. Grow one plant from seed and keep it alive all year." (2) **The balanced tail claims pace, not a trait the persona denies.** Its last sentence may not assert the opposite of any of the shown persona's three keywords (no "still let a peer share the weight" over the Twin, no "each venture gets finished" over the Horizon). Example, P154 (金_木): "…In balance, what you take on matches the strength you have to carry it. Your hunger and your stamina keep the same pace." Example, P169 (金_金): "…In balance, your strength is firm but never stiff. You keep your own standard without needing to defend it." (3) A Balanced page uses no catalyst passage that states a thin quantity (fixed by X2-03).

findings.criterion: house rule "don't assume a child, partner or boss" · A1
findings.quote: "Your partner gets all of your time and few of your words" (P023); "You feel more warmth than your partner ever gets to see" (P056); "You teach a child by doing the whole thing yourself … The child walks away" (P106); "Promotions you deserved have gone to louder people" (P017); "Where a raise is there for the asking … You lose the raise you never ask for" (P086); "You pass the need for permission to anyone under you" (P093); "With no one above you, you answer only to yourself" (P109–P111); "Your family does what you ask and keeps its ideas quiet" (P085)
findings.issue: The rule now in force is broken across 32 pages. The breaches follow the classical associations (the Steward's partner, the Magistrate's office, the Artisan's child), so they cluster by persona and recur on every element. For a single 22-year-old reader each of these lines is false, and the 金_金 remedy asserts the opposite (no boss) as a fact.
findings.fix: Sweep with a gate (flag partner, child, kid, boss, promotion, raise, colleague, team, meeting, under you, above you, household, your family outside the edge domain line). Substitutions: "the person you love" or "the one closest to you" for "your partner"; "whoever learns from you" or "anyone in your care" for "a child"; "the one in charge" or "whoever signs off" for the boss; "the next step up" for "promotion" or "raise". Example, `K2 金_食神 · catalyst.ledger[2].cost_others`: "You teach by doing the whole thing yourself. Your own way is the one you know works, and you show it rather than let a learner try another. You send whoever learns at your side away with a method that holds." Example, `PAIR 金_金 · advise_friction` diagnosis: "Answering only to yourself keeps your standard untested."

Add the per-chart rule: when two texts one chart shows draw on the same element, they take different acts of that element (Wood: begin, plant, add to; Fire: show, warm, gather; Earth: keep, tend, hold; Metal: cut, sort, finish; Water: rest, take in, wait). findings.issue: M4 is implemented as a filter on chip antonyms, and it fails in both directions. (a) When it filters out the second persona's keywords, the picker quietly takes a third keyword from the first persona. The page is then no longer 2+2, and on P063 it shows two drive angles and no cost to others from the Steward. On P063 the filter also removed "Keeps everything", which the page's own shared definition supports ("Holding it is how you feel secure, and over time you carry more than you finish"). (b) The real clashes sit in the motive sentence, which the filter does not read. The reader is told two opposite things about what makes them feel safe, or what they trust.
findings.fix: **Rule, two parts.** (1) The picker never takes a third keyword from one persona. If the second persona has no compatible keyword at its usual angle, it takes a compatible one at any angle. If none exists, the cell is flagged for one bridging passage, not filled silently. (2) The clash test reads the need clause ("… is your safety", "you need …", "you trust …") as well as the chip. Add Far-sighted × Loyal, Reads between lines × Knows what works, and Sets own bar × Better with rivals to the X-03 list. Where a swap is impossible (P066: every Steward keyword clashes with one Horizon keyword), rewrite the clashing motive instead. For example, Loyal's drive: "Being loyal costs you less than leaving ever would. Staying is how you show what matters, and you hold what is already yours instead of looking elsewhere. The people you stand by know exactly where to find you." For P084, the shared definition's last sentence becomes "You hold on to less of what you learn than you take in.", which is true of both personas.

findings.quote: "Having it near is what feels safe" (definition) beside "Having it within reach makes you feel safe" ("Keeps everything")
findings.issue: The same sentence frame appears twice on one screen. The M2 tail is meant to share no main act with its own persona's keywords. This is a repeated frame, not a restatement complaint.
findings.fix: "Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Earth gives it weight, so whatever you claim needs keeping. As a friction, what you own weighs more each year. You fill your hands with what you already have and leave no place for anything new."

findings.quote: "You pay for that rule in weight you carry by yourself." beside "You pay for that peace in closeness, one quiet evening at a time."
findings.issue: The same close frame ("You pay for that X in Y") appears twice on the page.
findings.fix: "Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Earth sets you solid and slow to shift. Running over, your strength feels like enough for anything, and owing nobody becomes the rule. You end up holding weight that others would have shared."

findings.quote: "You feel every loss as a blow to your standing. You would rather sit out a contest than risk losing it, because your standing feels at stake."
findings.issue: The reason repeats the claim, so the motive is circular. "standing" appears twice in one passage (three times on the page).
findings.fix: "Every loss lands as a blow to your standing. You would rather sit out a contest than risk losing it, since a low rank feels worse than no rank at all. You replay each defeat for weeks after the game is over."

findings.quote: "you hand them plenty one year"
findings.issue: "them" has no antecedent in the passage.
findings.fix: "You share each win rather than sit on it. Giving in bursts is your way of loving, and you hand the people around you plenty one year and nothing the next. Nobody near you ever doubts where your heart is."

findings.quote: "Where being hard to convince feels like being hard to fool"
findings.issue: "Where" is used as "because".
findings.fix: "You push back before you hear the end of a plan. To you, being hard to convince feels like being hard to fool, and you make people defend a plan instead of taking it. You take the ease out of every offer they bring you."

findings.quote: "Whenever you would rather show a result than explain a plan"
findings.issue: "Whenever" is used as "because" (a lasting preference is not an occasion).
findings.fix: "You prove an idea before you share it. Because you would rather show a result than explain a plan, you keep people out of it until it is done. Those close to you meet the work at the end and miss the making of it."

findings.quote: "you fix it rather than keeping the peace"
findings.issue: Broken parallel ("fix … rather than keep").
findings.fix: "When a rule stops making sense, you rewrite it with people still standing on it. Since you fix it rather than keep the peace, you change the footing with no warning. The rule you found pointless was somebody's floor."

findings.quote: "slow and solid … opens slowly … until it is solid"
findings.issue: "slow" and "solid" each appear twice in four sentences; only the persona tail changes.
findings.fix: "Your Expression is the gate where inner work becomes outer fact. Earth makes it slow and solid, made to last. As a catalyst, the gate opens late. Nothing of yours comes through until it is ready, and then it comes out blunt and complete."

findings.quote: "your world grows smaller each year"
findings.issue: "world" appears three times on the page (the head's "the world soaks in" and "The wider world reaches you"); only the tail changes.
findings.fix: "Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Earth holds it, and nothing you learn is lost. As a friction, the holding never stops. Familiar ground draws you in, every change looks like a threat, and your life grows smaller each year."

findings.quote: "you hold the yes or no … You hold up their next step"
findings.issue: "hold" appears four times on the page.
findings.fix: "Second-guessing an answer you already have leaves people waiting on it. Because being certain comes first, you sit on the yes or no for weeks rather than give a maybe. You stall their next step for as long as you second-guess."

findings.quote: "You would rather hold the pace"
findings.issue: "hold" appears four times on P088 and five on P165.
findings.fix: "Pushing through, you carry the people with you at your pace. You would rather keep your speed than slow it for someone, and that costs them the pause you never take. With you at the front, the group finishes what it started."

findings.quote: "the chance you spot long before it is near"
findings.issue: It repeats "long before" from "Far-sighted", which sits on every page that shows this edge.
findings.fix: "Earth runs through your wealth, your family and your social life. It is the chance you spot while it is still far off, the good year that becomes a gift for everyone at home, and the luck you hand round before it has cooled."

findings.quote: "the job you stay at until it is finished properly"
findings.issue: "stay" appears four times on the page, and "stay at a job until it is finished" mixes employment with a task.
findings.fix: "Earth runs through your wealth, your family and your career. It is the money put by that makes a bad month ordinary, the old chair you fix instead of buying a new one, and the job you see through to a proper finish."

findings.quote: "the skill you picked up alone"
findings.issue: "alone" appears three times on P082 and P164 ("alone with hunches", "happens alone").
findings.fix: "Earth runs through your mind, your growth and your career. It is the idea you work out in your own strange way, the skill you picked up without a teacher and kept to yourself, and the meaning you catch under the words in a meeting."

findings.quote: "Your load has grown past what one body can bear."
findings.issue: "body" appears three times in the remedy and four on P061 (with "the one body you have").
findings.fix: "Seek Wood, your own Body energy. Wood is the trunk under everything you reach for, the body that stands before it carries. Let it hold what Earth piles up. Your load has grown past what you can bear alone. Start each week with one thing that is only for you. Say no to one request before you say yes again."

findings.quote: "you make the saving on them"
findings.issue: Off-idiom.
findings.fix: "Spending on the people you love comes no easier than spending on yourself. Giving less feels safer than giving more, and you cut back on them first. You take what you save out of their share."

findings.quote: "Better with a rival, you turn a peer into one without asking."
findings.issue: The adjective phrase dangles at the opening.
findings.fix: "Because you do better with a rival, you turn a peer into one without asking. You would rather race someone than keep them company, and you hand a contest to a friend who wanted none. Your friends get faster just from standing next to you."

findings.quote: "the weight of the job that is yours because it never slips"
findings.issue: It does not parse: what never slips, the job or the weight?
findings.fix: "Earth runs through your family, your social life and your career. It is the promise at home kept without a reminder, the decision both sides of an argument can live with, and the work left in your hands because you never let it slip."

findings.pages: P156, P157, P158, P159, P160 (5 of 5 Fire Balanced pages; all 25 Balanced pages in the corpus use `advise_catalyst`)
findings.quote: P156: "In balance, the gate lets your work out when it is ready. Your warmth and wit reach people at the moment they count." then "Your light runs short, and what you make on your own rarely gets seen." P157: "In balance, the warmth holds steady and you spend no faster than you refill." then "putting back is the part you skip." P160: "In balance, the fire burns steady." then "Most of your chances are lost by never being claimed." Elsewhere: P167 "Your drive is short", P174 "What you have to give runs short", P175 "a reserve that was small to begin with".
findings.issue: M2 gave the Balanced chart its own definition, but THE ADVICE still renders the catalyst text, which opens by saying the energy runs short. The Balanced reader is told "Keep the mix." and that the energy is in balance, then told one box later that it is scarce. This is the "as a catalyst" problem from S5, moved down one section, and it shows on every Balanced page.
findings.fix: Rule: a Balanced chart's ADVICE renders `function.advise_balanced`, one per pair cell (25 texts). It opens on a keep-the-mix diagnosis, says what holds the balance, and then gives the acts. It may reuse the catalyst acts where they fit, under the M6 per-core budget. Interim, until the texts exist: on Balanced pages, render the catalyst advice without its first sentence. Samples. 火_火: "Your strength holds while what you put back keeps pace with what you spend. Ask one person for help on a job you usually do alone. Get two friends together once a month just for fun. Stand in the sun for ten minutes each morning." 木_火: "Your light reaches people when it counts, and it stays bright while you keep letting work out. Play an unfinished song to one friend. Post a drawing with the mistake left in." Balanced definitions also must not deny a cost that the ledger below them names (see F2-21, F2-22).

findings.pages: P057 here. Corpus: P057 and P135 (Horizon ×3, Steward ×0); P063 and P099 (Horizon ×3, Steward ×1); P006 (Twin ×3, Rival ×1); P150 (Twin ×2, Rival ×1, 3 keywords). 6 of 50 blend pages.
findings.quote: P057 is labelled "blend The Horizon+The Steward (2+2)". It shows "Chases the new", "Spends it fast" and "Looks past home", the same three passages as the Horizon page P055, under "Gain and loss fill your whole mind".
findings.issue: When the M4 antonym filter strikes one persona's keywords, the picker either fills from the other persona or shows three. The reader who has both faces equally meets only the chaser, and the "loss" half of the definition has nothing under it. M4 promised "two keywords from each persona", and 6 blend pages break it.
findings.fix: Rule: the picker searches every 2+2 combination of the two personas' keywords on that pole and takes the first set with no antonym pair. Only when no such set exists does it fall back, and then to X-03(b): the clashing pair shown with the fixed hinge line. It never fills from the other persona and never shows fewer than four. For P057 a clean set appears to exist: "Chases the new" and "Looks past home" (Horizon) with "Counts everything" and "Holds back" (Steward). This needs checking against the antonym table, which is not in the audit pages.

findings.quote: "Fire makes it light, so whatever you do shows. … What little shows comes out as warmth." (P034)
findings.issue: The head says everything shows; the catalyst tail and the advice say little shows. The contradiction sits inside one four-sentence definition. "Makes it light" also reads as "not heavy".
findings.fix: Head sentence 2 becomes "Fire lights it, and what you make can reach people." The pair field (the blend text) in full: "Your Expression is the gate where inner work becomes outer fact. Fire lights it, and what you make can reach people. As a catalyst, the light runs short. Your warmth and wit flare in the moment and fade, and little of it lasts once the evening is over."

findings.quote: "Your light runs short, and what you make on your own rarely gets seen."
findings.issue: The diagnosis fits the Artisan only. On P035 it sits beside "Being seen doing it matters more to you than doing it" and an edge where "the table … turns toward you". M2 asks for a neutral diagnosis that holds for both personas.
findings.fix: "Your light runs short, and little of what you make is still there the next day. Play an unfinished song to one friend. Post a drawing with the mistake left in. Bring one thing you made to the next gathering."

findings.quote: "and you spend the shared money on the evening"
findings.issue: Spending money that belongs to two people is a charge of misuse, and it assumes a joint purse with a partner or household. BIZ_04 and the house rule both rule this out.
findings.fix: "Whenever a plan with others meets your pleasure, you choose the pleasure. You would rather have a good time now than keep a promise later, and tonight wins. You leave them short on the plans you made together."

findings.quote: "What you need from the people close to you is watching more than joining in. You feel company only once it is facing you"
findings.issue: Sentence 1 has to be parsed twice: who watches, and who joins? "Feel company" is not idiomatic.
findings.fix: "Even with close friends, you want an audience more than a companion. Company feels real to you only once it is facing you, and you turn a friend into a crowd. You take their evening and give back a show instead."

findings.quote: "Staying uncorrected is a rule you keep at a price. … a peer's version … the same mistake"
findings.issue: The opener is stilted ("uncorrected" is above B2) and announces the price instead of naming the need. "Mistake" appears three times on the page with the remedy.
findings.fix: "A peer's correction stings more than being wrong. You repeat your own mistake rather than take their version, since yours at least stays yours. You end up paying for the same mistake twice, and the second time you pay alone."

findings.quote: "Even beside a friend you never switch off, handing them a race instead of yourself."
findings.issue: This is a participial tail (house rule B4), and "beside" comes back in the next sentence. The middle sentence stays as it is.
findings.fix: "Even with a friend you never switch off, and you bring a race where they wanted company. Being ahead counts more with you than being beside someone, so you set the pace even on a walk. You keep from them a friend with nothing to prove."

findings.quote: "you are all in unasked … Your money makes their plan bigger and riskier than they chose."
findings.issue: "All in unasked" is awkward. "Than they chose" echoes the victim close BIZ_04 struck ("a race they never chose to run").
findings.fix: "With someone you like, you go all in without being asked. You would rather add your own money than check whether they wanted it, and you double what they put in. You leave them with a plan bigger and riskier than the one they made."

findings.quote: "You give a friend's dare your full speed before they take it back."
findings.issue: "Before they take it back" leaves the reader asking what is taken back. The sentence needs a second read. The middle sentence stays.
findings.fix: "You take up a friend's dare at full speed, before they can laugh it off. Winning in front of a friend matters more than keeping it friendly, so you play every round for keeps. You never let a game stay just a game."

findings.quote: "Other people's ambition is the kind you catch fastest. You catch a rival's goal faster … rather than wait."
findings.issue: "Catch" appears 3 times and "fast" twice, and "rather than wait" has no object (wait for what?). The middle frame stays; only its tail gains the object.
findings.fix: "Your ambition often starts out as someone else's. You catch a rival's goal faster than you find your own, so you run on borrowed wanting rather than wait for yours. You are hungry for a contest worth your whole heart."

findings.quote: "Your partner and friends get days of silence with no word on why."
findings.issue: This assumes a partner, which the house rule forbids. The middle sentence stays.
findings.fix: "Working something out, you go quiet on everyone around you. Because you think best alone rather than with others, you leave the people beside you on their own. You give those closest to you days of silence with no word on why."

findings.quote: "push too hard … push through … spent pushing … strength … strength … week … week"
findings.issue: Push 3 times, strength twice, week twice and spend twice in 37 words. This is the one passage on the Metal pages that drags. (It is filed under C, not A3.) The middle sentence stays.
findings.fix: "Each time you push too hard, you draw on strength you do not have. You would rather push through than keep the energy to finish the week. By the weekend you are short on sleep and on everything you meant to save."

findings.quote: "Because one exception feels like a collapse starting … You keep everyone at home in line"
findings.issue: "A collapse starting" is awkward. "Keep everyone in line" passes a disciplinarian verdict on the reader where BIZ_04 wants the act. "At home" assumes a household.
findings.fix: "Keeping to the rules is how you look after others. Because one exception feels like the first crack, you give them the rule instead of what they asked for. You hold your people to the letter and take from them the ease of being wrong."

findings.quote: "Where titles are concerned … a colleague … Colleagues climb the slow way, with no help from you."
findings.issue: Both Magistrate passages on the page open on "Where". "Colleague" appears twice. "With no help from you" reads as a charge of withholding. The middle sentence stays.
findings.fix: "When it comes to titles, you make everyone earn theirs too. Since an unearned rank looks like cheating, you give a colleague the long route rather than a quiet word. You leave them to climb the slow way."

findings.quote: "you hold everyone to every one they make. Your friends have their offhand words held to the letter."
findings.issue: "Everyone to every one" is a word game the eye trips on. The close is passive, and "hold/held" appear twice.
findings.fix: "To you, a passing promise is one to keep. Because a promise is a rule rather than a wish, you hold others to theirs as tightly as you hold yourself. You treat a friend's offhand words as a contract."

findings.quote: "your partner gets the careful share only. You feel more warmth than your partner ever gets to see."
findings.issue: This assumes a partner, twice. The middle frame stays; only the noun changes.
findings.fix: "You hold back hardest where you love most. You keep a reserve rather than give it all, and the person closest to you gets the careful share only. You feel more warmth than they ever get to see."

findings.quote: "You show up daily whether your partner needs it that day or not."
findings.issue: This assumes a partner, and "daily … that day" doubles. The middle sentence stays.
findings.fix: "You show up every day for those you love, needed or not. Being there makes you feel useful, so you offer presence where a question would serve better. You give them your company without fail and seldom the thing they wanted."

findings.quote: "You keep love going on time … so you give your partner steady warmth … Home life with you"
findings.issue: It assumes a partner and a shared home, and "keep love going on time" is not idiomatic.
findings.fix: "You keep love going, steadily and without fail. Since reliable feels more like love to you than exciting does, you give those close to you steady warmth over surprise. You offer them everything except the unexpected."

findings.quote: "Most of your chances are lost by never being claimed, not by failing. Tell three people about the venture you have in mind."
findings.issue: The diagnosis fits the Steward. On P058 it sits under "you move while the chance is only a guess" and "Your friends hear about the good openings from you", so it tells the Horizon to do what the page says she already does. "Tell three people about the venture" also repeats 水_木's "Tell one person about a plan you have kept quiet". A strong Water core shows both on one chart.
findings.fix: "What you build earns less than it should, since you seldom ask to be paid for it. Name your price once and hold to it. Put one idea in front of a real buyer this month."

findings.quote: "Fire makes it warm, so what you build reaches people in time."
findings.issue: "In time" is unclear: eventually, or before it is too late? Round 1 filed it (F-38); it is still live.
findings.fix: Head sentence 2 becomes "Fire makes it warm, and people feel what you build." The pair field (the blend text) in full: "Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Fire makes it warm, and people feel what you build. As a catalyst, the warmth runs short, and you want a far chance as much as steady pay. You lose most on what you leave unclaimed."

findings.quote: "You learn from others and still make each idea your own."
findings.issue: The Balanced definition denies the cost the ledger names directly below it ("Self-taught is the only learning you trust"; "Thinks best alone").
findings.fix: "Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Fire makes it warm, and you keep what lights you up. In balance, what you take in warms you without weighing you down. Whatever you learn, you turn into your own."

findings.quote: "You answer to fair rules and hold your rank without strain."
findings.issue: It contradicts "Being in charge weighs on you once you take it … Nobody thinks to ask how you are holding up" on the same page.
findings.fix: "Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Fire fuels it, and outside demands shape you. In balance, demands come at a pace you can meet. You answer to rules you find fair, and your rank keeps pace with your work."

findings.quote: "Rest one full day a week with no work at all." / "You mistake being unstoppable for being well."
findings.issue: A strong Fire core shows this remedy and the 火_水 catalyst advice ("Leave an hour empty between two big jobs") on one chart, so the rest act appears twice in one core. The verb "mistake" also collides with "Won't be told" ("the same mistake twice") on P037 and P039.
findings.fix: "Seek Water, the Order energy. Water runs cool and keeps to its banks, and a blaze meets it only on the water's terms. Let it shape what your Fire burns. You take being unstoppable for being well. Hand the lead on one shared job to someone else this month. Let someone finish speaking before you answer."

findings.quote: "You do your best work when someone is allowed to tell you no. Ask someone you respect to grade one piece of your work"
findings.issue: A strong Metal core also shows 金_金's remedy ("Say your plan to a person who can refuse it. Share one unfinished piece of work with three people") and 金_土's ("Send the rough draft before the clean one exists"). One chart then gets "submit your work to be judged" three times, and "someone allowed to tell you no" twice.
findings.fix: "You do your best work when someone else sets the bar. Join one team where another person calls the plays. Say your doubt out loud the next time a plan is agreed too fast."

findings.quote: "Take one slow weekend. Let the numbers wait."
findings.issue: A weak Water core shows this remedy and 水_水's catalyst advice ("Rest a full day after any big push") on one chart: two rest acts. "Slow" also appears twice ("slow fill", "slow weekend").
findings.fix: "Seek Water, your own Body energy. Water is the deep you draw from, the sleep and food and slow fill that come before anything is lit. Let it cool what Fire burns. Whether you are reaching for more or guarding what you have, the heat comes out of your own reserves. Leave the money alone for one evening a week." (60 words)

findings.quote: "Gives easily" (Horizon)
findings.issue: It is a near-twin of the Artisan's "Gives first", "Gives freely", "Gives too much" and "Gives it away". A strong Water core shows "Gives easily" (Fire, Horizon) and "Gives first" (Wood, Artisan) on one chart, so two personas read as one.
findings.fix: Rename the chip "Open-handed", which the Horizon already uses on Metal; no reader meets both. Keep the passage.

findings.quote: "Practicing alone"
findings.issue: US spelling in a British corpus ("favour"; P036 "practise").
findings.fix: "Without an audience, you will not start. Practising alone feels like wasted effort, and you save the real work for a crowd rather than do it unseen. You lose the quiet practice that your talent needs most to grow."

findings.quote: "You never feel enough as a real amount"
findings.issue: "Feel X as Y" is not English (round 1 fixed the same slip in F-12). It also makes a second "You never" on the page.
findings.fix: "You overdo it, and you know it while you do. Since enough never feels like a real amount to you, you push a thing past its best rather than stop there. You are allowed to stop where a thing is at its best."

findings.quote: "Fast enough to finish other people's sentences, you usually do."
findings.issue: The opener has no subject for "fast", so it needs a second read. "Usually" also closes "Speaks up" on the same page.
findings.fix: "You think fast enough to finish other people's sentences, and often you do. Waiting for a thought to end feels like wasted time, and you answer before hearing it all. Slower thinkers lose the last part of their point to your reply."

findings.quote: "rather keep your footing than be held up"
findings.issue: Next to "match your pace", "held up" first reads as "delayed", not "supported".
findings.fix: "You trust closeness only side by side, so you let a friend near once they match your pace. You would rather keep your footing than be carried, even when you need it. On your hard days, nobody is close enough to catch you."

findings.quote: "because you would rather keep moving than stop to refill"
findings.issue: On P042 "would rather" appears 3 times, twice as "would rather keep" ("Side by side": "You would rather keep your footing").
findings.fix: "Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Fire makes it warm, so you recover by doing. Running thin, the reserve goes first, because you keep moving instead of stopping to refill. You pay for each bright day with a tired one."

findings.quote: "Your Mind feeds on what it finds by itself"
findings.issue: "Your Mind" opens three sentences on the page (definition ×2, advice).
findings.fix: Tail: "As a catalyst, little teaching reaches you. You feed on what you find by yourself, and insight arrives in flashes with nobody there to share it." (Assembled: "Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Fire makes it warm, and you keep what lights you up. As a catalyst, little teaching reaches you. You feed on what you find by yourself, and insight arrives in flashes with nobody there to share it.")

findings.quote: "Your Mind learns to manage without it"
findings.issue: "Your Mind" again opens three sentences on the page.
findings.fix: "Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Fire makes it warm, and you keep what lights you up. As a catalyst, little warmth or teaching reaches you. You learn to manage without it, and what you understand you reached on your own."

findings.quote: "Once a month go to a talk … Keep one person to ask the simple question, and ask it."
findings.issue: A comma is missing after the opening phrase, and "keep one person to ask" does not parse on first reading.
findings.fix: "Your Mind grows on warmth, and warmth is something you have to go and sit near. Once a month, go to a talk or a workshop just to take it in. Choose one person you can ask the simple questions, and ask them."

findings.quote: "you hold back the honest read they needed. They walk away with your warmth and without your honest view."
findings.issue: "Honest" and "read" each appear twice in two sentences.
findings.fix: "Your first read of anyone is a kind one. Because you would rather keep a person warm than judge them out loud, you hold back the truth they needed. You leave them with your warmth and without your honest view."

findings.quote: "You look after people … so you look after their comfort"
findings.issue: "Look after" appears 3 times, counting the chip. The middle's joint is the live text, unchanged.
findings.fix: "You look after people without being asked. Keeping the people near you sheltered is how you feel at ease, so you put their comfort before yours. Under your roof, everyone breathes out."

findings.quote: "you lean on theirs rather than build any"
findings.issue: "Build any" leaves its noun to be guessed.
findings.fix: "The care you give so freely is also the care you lean on in return. Because another person's steadiness feels more reliable than yours, you lean on theirs rather than build your own. You go without the one kind of strength you cannot borrow."

findings.quote: "you catch it … letting them meet it … managing it"
findings.issue: "Catch it" is unclear (the fall? the mistake?), and three "it"s point at different things.
findings.fix: "Each time a loved one is about to fail, you step in. Protecting them from the consequence feels more like love to you than letting them meet it. With every rescue, you keep from them the small win of managing on their own."

findings.quote: "ground that does not catch. Let it ground what Fire burns."
findings.issue: "Ground" appears in two sentences in a row, first as a noun and then as a verb.
findings.fix: "Seek Earth, the Mind energy. Earth takes the blaze in and keeps the warmth, soil that does not catch. Let it ground what Fire burns. You answer to pressure faster than you recover from it. Stay with one hard feeling for ten minutes before you act on it. Tend one plant or one friendship with no goal attached."

findings.quote: "You feel safer in charge alone than sharing it"
findings.issue: The parallel is broken ("in charge alone" against "sharing it"). The middle's joint is the live text, unchanged.
findings.fix: "Being in charge weighs on you once you take it. You feel safer running things alone than sharing them, so you are rarely carried. Nobody thinks to ask how you are holding up."

findings.quote: "so you let the book decide what you knew"
findings.issue: The tenses clash (round 1 F-31; still live).
findings.fix: "Where the book and your judgment part, you side with the book. You want it done in order more than your way, so you let the book overrule what you already knew. Chances that needed a quick call pass you by."

findings.quote: "By the book is the only way you trust a thing done."
findings.issue: "By the book" as a subject, plus the missing "to be", makes the sentence need a second read.
findings.fix: "You trust a thing only when it is done by the book. Since an outside rule steadies you, you go by the book over the shortcut. Your work is the standard others get checked against."

findings.quote: "Your friendships are decades old"
findings.issue: This is false for most readers aged 18 to 35, and the reading cannot know it.
findings.fix: "Keeping a thing going is the warmest part of you. You would rather keep one thing warm for years than start many, since what lasts feels real to you. Your oldest friendships still hold."

findings.quote: "Gain and loss fill your whole mind"
findings.issue: On an Action page, lower-case "mind" reads as the Mind function, which for a Water core is Metal.
findings.fix: "Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Fire turns it bright, lit the moment a chance appears. As a friction, the light burns through its fuel. Gain and loss fill your thoughts, and little of you is left to rest."

findings.pages: P166 to P170 (5 of 5 Metal Balanced pages); corpus check: 25 of 25 Balanced pages
findings.quote: P167: "In balance, you claim what you can carry and see it through" over THE ADVICE "Your drive is short, and each piece of it needs a clear place to go." P170: "In balance, the test is quick and fair. What passes it settles in" over "You let in less than the world has to offer, and the gap shows…". It opens on a neutral line that names what keeps this energy in balance, for example 水_金: "What you take in is tested and then trusted, and that balance is worth keeping." findings.pages: All 35 Metal pages carry one of these texts; 9 of the 10 Metal advice and remedy texts repeat an act that the same reader also gets on another energy page
findings.quote: **Weak Wood** (Metal friction, Water catalyst): "Give one evening a week to learning something nobody grades" (木_金) and "Take one free course on a subject that is new to you" (木_水). **Balanced or strong Wood**: "Join one class that meets at a set time" with the same free course; "Set a weekly time with a friend to train or practise together" with 木_木 "Start one weekly session that builds your strength" and 木_土 "give it the same hour each week. Tell one friend about it and ask them to check on you". **Strong Fire**: "Choose one aim for this month and cross two others off" (火_金) and "Choose one idea to finish and drop the rest" (火_木 friction). **Strong Earth**: "Give one thing you made to someone this month" (土_金) and "Pass on one thing you learned to someone who needs it" (土_火 friction). **Weak Earth**: "See one show as a guest, not a critic" (土_金) and "go to a talk or a workshop just to take it in" (土_火 catalyst). **Strong Metal**: "Share one unfinished piece of work with three people" (金_金) and "Send the rough draft before the clean one exists" (金_土 friction); "Say your plan to a person who can refuse it" and "Ask someone you respect to grade one piece of your work" (金_火 catalyst). **Weak Metal**: "Cut one commitment this month that drains more than it gives" (金_金) and "Drop one project you no longer believe in. Choose three things for this month and turn down the others" (金_木 friction). **Strong Water**: "Share one rough idea with a group this week" (水_金), "Tell one person about a plan you have kept quiet" (水_木) and "Tell three people about the venture you have in mind" (水_火). **Weak Water**: "collect three answers before you decide" (水_金) and "Ask a friend for the whole answer rather than guessing it" (水_水). Corpus-wide, "Clear out one drawer…" opens a step in both 木_金 and 火_金, although the M6 gate claims no step repeats anywhere.
findings.issue: M6 passed its gate, but the gate counted only a fixed list of act families (sleep, eat, sit, read, deadline, elder, above, child, write, walk, call, money). The acts that recur are outside that list: share unfinished work, tell people a plan, take a class, cut or drop a commitment, choose one and drop the rest, go to a show or talk, pass something on, ask for a fuller answer, and a fixed weekly slot. A reader who opens their five energy pages meets the same prescription twice or three times in other words. That is the defect M6 was meant to remove.
findings.fix: Rule: judge M6 by the act itself, not by a family list, and check it per **reader set**, not per core. For each core there are three sets: weak (Body and Mind catalysts, the other three frictions), strong (the reverse) and Balanced (five catalysts, or five balanced advices once MT2-01 lands). Within a set each act appears once. Add these families to the gate: share or tell (an idea, a plan, unfinished work), class/course/skill, cut/drop/turn down, choose one and drop the rest, attend (show, talk, workshop), give or pass on, ask for the answer, fixed weekly slot, training session. Example swaps for the Metal texts: 木_金 friction "Give one evening a week to learning something nobody grades." → "Read one book for nothing but the pleasure of it." (no read act in the Wood core; 59 words). 火_金 catalyst "Choose one aim for this month and cross two others off." → "Cancel one subscription you have stopped noticing." (Metal cuts; 44 words). Re-run the gate on the other seven before choosing which side of each pair changes.

findings.quote: "The bar rises each time you clear it, and rest never comes."
findings.issue: On P093 "Never off duty" closes on "You lose the rest your free evenings were meant to give you". The page names lost rest twice, against the M6 rule "Lost rest is the cost in at most one passage per page". (P091 is borderline: "You wear out long before the work does" sits beside the same close.)
findings.fix: "Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal turns it exact, a line over your growth. As a friction, the line turns inward, because order is where you feel safe. The bar rises each time you clear it, and enough never comes." (50)

findings.quote: "Each time the rule goes first, you take away their fair hearing."
findings.issue: "Fair hearing" charges the reader with being unfair. BIZ_04 asks the cost to others to name what the act takes, not what kind of person it makes the reader.
findings.fix: "Unsure of someone, you put the rule first. A rule treats everyone the same, and you apply it before the person's case. Each time the rule goes first, you hear their side of it last." (35)

findings.quote: "You pass the need for permission to anyone under you. Permission from above is the only yes you take, and you send their questions up rather than answer."
findings.issue: It assumes the reader has people under them and someone above them, which is the boss assumption the house rules ban. The "answer" here also brings the word to ×6 on P093.
findings.fix: "You pass your need for permission on to whoever comes to you. Your own yes never feels like enough, and you look for a higher one before you say it. You leave them waiting on a permission you were free to give." (42)

findings.quote: "Where you avoid change, you avoid it for two. … You avoid change so well that your partner goes without any too."
findings.issue: It assumes a partner ("for two", "your partner"). "so well that" reads as a sneer, and the close repeats the opener. (Round 1 MT-19 named the close; it was skipped as A3, but the partner rule now applies.)
findings.fix: "Where you avoid change, you avoid it for others too. The agreed plan feels safe to you, and you keep those you love inside it instead of letting them change it. You hold back the new starts they wanted to make." (41)

findings.quote: "You keep a partner on the safe plan rather than their wanted one … You take from your partner the risks that were theirs to choose."
findings.issue: It assumes a partner twice, and "their wanted one" is not idiomatic.
findings.fix: "For the ones you love, playing safe is the rule too. Their risk feels like your own, and you steer them to the safe plan over the one they wanted. You take from them the risks that were theirs to choose." (41)

findings.quote: "Your first try already looks right, and they see the ease without the care behind it. You teach them to aim no higher than what you settle for."
findings.issue: The same page's drive says "A thing has to be right in every detail before it pleases you". The reader is a perfectionist and someone who settles on one page. The passage itself says there is care behind the ease and then says the reader settles. (Round 1 MT-24; the M5 rewrite softened it but kept "settle".)
findings.fix: "Whenever you take it easy, you take people with you. Your skill makes hard work look light, and those near you copy the ease without the care behind it. You pass on the ease and leave them without the craft." (40)

findings.quote: "Talking back comes first in you. … You spend your talking back on small rules and have none left for big ones."
findings.issue: "spend your talking back" uses the chip as a noun and has to be read twice. "comes first in you" is vague.
findings.fix: "Talking back is your first move. A rule you did not agree to feels like being pushed around, and you argue before you ask what it is for. You use up your fight on small rules and have none left for the big ones." (44)

findings.quote: "Since getting the choice right matters more to you than being on time, you let the warm moment pass. Underneath it, you want to be known as someone who truly listens."
findings.issue: The close does not follow. Nothing in "Chooses well" is about listening. "the warm moment" has no referent.
findings.fix: "For you, a good choice beats a fast one. Getting it right matters more to you than being on time, and the moment often passes while you weigh it. Underneath, you want to look back and still be glad of what you picked." (43)

findings.quote: "You teach a child by doing the whole thing yourself. … The child walks away with a method that holds"
findings.issue: It assumes the reader has or teaches a child, and the close's subject is the child.
findings.fix: "You teach by doing the whole thing yourself. Your own way is the one you know works, and you show it to a beginner rather than let them try another. You send them off with a method that holds, learned at your side." (43)

findings.quote: "With Metal running over, you live on comparison more than company"
findings.issue: The element's quantity is given as the cause, which the house rule now bans. Round 1 let it pass before that rule existed. "company" also repeats the definition close on P110.
findings.fix: "You keep an exact score with everyone you like. Comparison steadies you more than friendship does, and you keep a quiet tally of who gave more. Keep in mind that you wanted the closeness long before you wanted the score." (40)

findings.quote: "Hating to lose even a game is how you show you care. Since you want the win more than the evening, you keep arguing after it ends."
findings.issue: Nothing on the page supports "how you show you care", and wanting the win over the evening undercuts it. "it" could be the win, the evening or the game. (Round 1 MT-09, approved as A1/A2, still open in this part.)
findings.fix: "Losing even a small game feels like losing ground to you. You want the win more than the evening, and you keep arguing after the final score. You cost the people you play with the fun of the game." (39)

findings.quote: "Metal piles up in you, so your bets run on nerve to spare and caution borrowed."
findings.issue: The element is the cause, and "caution borrowed" does not mean anything plain. (Round 1 MT-08, approved, still open.) The close is good and stays in substance.
findings.fix: "Your bets are sized to the thrill more than the margin. A big stake is where you feel most awake, and caution never gets a vote. You bet the rent on a feeling that fades long before the bill does." (40)

findings.quote: "the quiet line at the door built on for months"
findings.issue: The image cannot be pictured. A line at a door, built on for months, gives no clear thing in the Mind domain.
findings.fix: "Metal runs through your family, your mind and your health. It is the secret told at home that stops with you, the subject learned to its last page and built on for good, and the old habit that keeps you steady through a hard year."

findings.quote: "you give the ones who tell you everything nothing of yourself back"
findings.issue: The word order makes readers parse it twice. (Round 1 MT-38; its fix closed on an instruction and was superseded by M1, so the middle stayed.)
findings.fix: "You keep your own troubles as closely as everyone else's. You would rather hold things than need holding, and the people who tell you everything hear nothing of yours. Your closest friends see your calm face and never your worries." (40)

findings.quote: "In balance, you claim what you can carry and see it through."
findings.issue: The Balanced page then shows "Starts fast" ("your patience runs out somewhere in the middle") and "Spots the opening" ("you spot a newer opening while you are claiming this one"). The definition promises the follow-through the keywords deny.
findings.fix: "Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Metal makes it exact, so what you take on ends finished or not at all. In balance, you go after only what is worth the strength it takes. What comes in is enjoyed, and some of it stays." (49)

findings.quote: "You stand on your own and still let a peer share the weight."
findings.issue: The Balanced Twin page then says "you build alone rather than with help" and "Recovers alone".
findings.fix: "Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Metal makes it hard, and your will holds. In balance, your strength is firm but never stiff. You stand on your own and still bend when a peer has the better case." (43)

findings.quote: "In balance, the test is quick and fair."
findings.issue: The Balanced Alchemist page then says "you are slow to be glad" and "Real kindness reaches you late". "Quick" is the one word that clashes.
findings.fix: "Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Metal turns it exact, and what you take in is tested before it is kept. In balance, the test is fair and it ends. What passes it settles in, and you trust it enough to use it." (48)

findings.quote: "because standing down feels unsafe"
findings.issue: "stand down" is repeated on the page ("The alert in you never stands down"); there is an obvious swap.
findings.fix: "Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal turns it exact, a line over your growth. As a friction, the line cuts deeper than any task asks, because easing off feels unsafe. You wear out long before the work does."

findings.quote: "you spend a free evening on duty … the rest your free evenings were meant to give you"
findings.issue: "free evening" twice in one passage.
findings.fix: "Off duty is a state you never fully manage. The alert in you never stands down, and you spend a free evening on duty rather than inside it. You lose the rest your evenings off were meant to give you."

findings.quote: "Your rank was built one rule at a time."
findings.issue: "rank" ×4 and "time" ×5 on the page, and the edge ends "a proper step at a time". The passive also leaves the reader out.
findings.fix: "Your Order is the rules you answer to and the rank you hold by them. Metal makes it hard and exact, the finish growth needs. As a catalyst, the line runs faint and you draw it yourself. You built your standing one rule after another."

findings.quote: "small tasks take the care big ones deserved"
findings.issue: Tense slip in a present-tense statement.
findings.fix: "Properly is the one speed you own. You do every step properly rather than good enough, and small tasks take the care big ones deserve. Your evenings go to jobs that nobody would ever check."

findings.quote: "and the last one rarely pays"
findings.issue: "the last one" reads as "the final chance" as easily as "the one before".
findings.fix: "Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Metal keeps it exact, and nothing you claim counts until it is finished. As a friction, you claim far more than you see through. Your freedom lives in the next chance, and the one in hand rarely pays off."

findings.quote: "You spend your strength on what you claim before yourself"
findings.issue: "before yourself" reads first as time ("before you claim yourself"), then as priority.
findings.fix: "Seek Fire, your own Body energy. Fire is warmth kept in, the fuel and rest that keep a light lit before it works on anything. Let it hold what Metal spends. You spend your strength on your claims, not yourself, and tired is where you make your worst deals. Eat warm food daily. Talk deals through with a friend." (59)

findings.quote: "the chance you watched another take"
findings.issue: "another" alone as a pronoun is stiff at B1 to B2.
findings.fix: "Playing it safe keeps you out of the loss column and the win column. You take the known small wage rather than the unknown better one, since playing safe is never judged. You pay for playing it safe in the chance you watched others take."

findings.quote: "You feel money that sits is a chance going cold"
findings.issue: The sentence has to be parsed twice ("feel money" before the clause resolves).
findings.fix: "Spending it all is your first instinct. Money left to sit feels like a chance going cold, and you spend it all on the next thing rather than keep it. Remember that you are allowed to let money sit until the right chance comes."

findings.quote: "Your eye finds the door before anyone else sees a wall."
findings.issue: The idiom is a door *where* others see a wall; "before" breaks it.
findings.fix: "You spot the opening when it is only a gap. You wake more for a far chance than a near one, and you spot a newer opening while you are claiming this one. Your eye finds a door where everyone else sees a wall."

findings.quote: "What leaves your hands has already passed…"
findings.issue: "leave(s)" ×4 and "hands" ×4 on P108; THE ADVICE also says "little ever leaves your hands".
findings.fix: "Setting the bar is something you do unasked. A standard you did not choose bores you, so you set your own rather than keep the given one, and hold yourself to it. Anything you finish has already passed the hardest judge it will meet."

findings.quote: "you defend a position rather than learn from it"
findings.issue: "it" points to the position, not to the teaching.
findings.fix: "Whenever someone tries to teach you, you check the messenger first. Since being right is how you stay safe, you defend your position rather than learn from theirs. You lose every lesson that needed you to be wrong before it could teach you."

findings.quote: "Wanting to know where you stand costs you the company you wanted."
findings.issue: "want" ×5 on P110; two of them are in this one sentence.
findings.fix: "Your Body is the strength the whole of you stands on. Metal keeps it exact, so your standard holds. Running over, your will needs a contest and finds one wherever you go. Wanting to know where you stand costs you the company you came for."

findings.quote: "Trusting nerve more than math"
findings.issue: US "math" in a corpus that writes "practise" and "favours".
findings.fix: "Where the bet is biggest, you are calmest, and you take that as a sign. Trusting nerve more than numbers, you bet with the rent before the sums are done. You come out of that calm short on rent and short on sleep."

findings.quote: "You return recovered rather than being seen recovering"
findings.issue: Broken parallel after "rather than".
findings.fix: "Recovering alone spares the people near you your worst days. You return recovered rather than be seen recovering, and give them the finished version only. Your closest people meet you only on your good days."

findings.quote: "after the work … the work runs on … before the work begins"
findings.issue: "work" three times in 39 words. (Apply after MT2-02 if that changes "Cut one commitment".)
findings.fix: "You treat rest as something you earn after the work instead of the thing the work runs on. Cut one commitment this month that drains more than it gives. Decide your stopping time before you start, and stop there."

findings.quote: "You need them safe more than you need them tried"
findings.issue: At B1 to B2 "tried" reads as "attempted"; the sense is "tested".
findings.fix: "Protective is your instinct with the people you love. You need them safe more than you need them tested, so you step in before letting them fall. You are protecting them from the one thing that would have taught them."

findings.quote: "until it is a result for others. Working it out alone comes easier to you than together"
findings.issue: "a result for others" is stiff, and "than together" leaves the comparison unfinished.
findings.fix: "Your thinking stays private until it is done. Working it out alone comes easier to you than working it out together, and the people near you get only the conclusion. They meet your plans finished, with no part in the making of them."
